name: Tide
line: One thin horizon organises the page: the hero is a moonlit fjord with its horizon at 56% and the headline above it, then every section sets its title and pictures in the sky and its text in the sea, with smoker and non-smoker risk rising from the line as two to-scale masts with reflections, the two networks floating above it, and the page ground moving from day through late afternoon to dusk and night as you scroll.
notes: The day-to-dusk shift is a small inline script that interpolates the body colour between tone anchors; light sections hold their tone and the switch to dark happens only while the sunset photograph fills the screen, so text never sits on a mid-tone. Without JavaScript each section shows its own static tone. The masts use one scale (2.5 px per person in 1,000 on desktop). Ibarra Real Nova has no Cyrillic; Hanken Grotesk has Cyrillic-ext only, so the RU site would need other faces.
